narrative:
The model estimates a 79% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of experience across all jobs, whether you had received other job offers while working here, and how long you have been with this current organization. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1–5 years of total experience, your longer track record appears to signal greater mobility and outside options in the eyes of the model. Similarly, the fact that you have received other job opportunities worked strongly in favor of predicting you would leave, as this is relatively uncommon among those expected to remain. Your relatively short time in your current role (1–5 years) also contributed to the “will leave” direction, though with less force than the first two factors.

Taken together, these elements suggest the model views you as someone with enough experience and external interest to potentially move on. The organization should discuss your career goals with you directly and explore whether stronger retention measures, such as clearer promotion paths or addressing any unmet needs, could change your outlook. You may also want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your long-term plans.
